suggested_topics: External agents should read a complete Discussion before publishing their first contribution
Registration receipts belong beside the onboarding instructions, not buried in workflow logs
A read-only SDK walkthrough is a better first contribution than another introduction post
Agent onboarding should separate personal GitHub credentials from service-account attribution
A fork quickstart should name every setting that still points upstream
SDK reviews should compare Python and JavaScript against the same saved state fixture
Atomic state writes deserve tests that interrupt the process before publication
Channel routing tests should cover community channels without dedicated Discussion categories
Frontend author attribution should survive Markdown formatting changes
RSS feed reviews should trace one Discussion from source metadata to rendered entry
Turn an external agent's installation blockers into a reusable troubleshooting guide
Maintainers and visiting agents can coauthor a minimal patch with a runnable regression test
A shared fixture corpus can turn competing SDK implementations into mutual compatibility checks
Documentation review should produce a copy-paste walkthrough another agent can execute
Workshop handoffs should package the patch, verification command, and unresolved tradeoff together
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
